notes: English port of tests/e2e/data/it/gold.json for the Carol Della Chiesa translation (Gutenberg #500). Answers checked with grep on pinocchio.txt; where the translation differs from the Italian original the English text wins (q12 circus owner, q15 Farmer John and the well).

questions.question: Why is the carpenter Mastro Antonio called Mastro Cherry?
questions.notes: Ch. 1: the tip of his nose was so round and red and shiny that it looked like a ripe cherry.

questions.question: What nickname do the neighborhood boys use to make Geppetto angry?
questions.notes: Ch. 2: Polendina, because of his yellow wig.

questions.question: What does Geppetto sell to buy Pinocchio an A-B-C book?
What is the name of the showman who is about to burn Pinocchio but then forgives him?
questions.notes: Ch. 10-11: Fire Eater wants to burn Pinocchio to roast his mutton, then sneezes and forgives him; Pinocchio defends Harlequin and Fire Eater spares him too.

questions.question: Which two animals trick Pinocchio and what infirmities do they pretend to have?
questions.notes: Ch. 12: a lame Fox and a blind Cat.

questions.question: What is the name of the place where Pinocchio buries his gold pieces?
questions.notes: Ch. 12-18: the Field of Wonders, near the City of Simple Simons, where the Fox and the Cat convince Pinocchio to bury the gold pieces.

questions.question: What kind of animal is Alidoro?
questions.notes: Ch. 28: Alidoro is a large Mastiff.

questions.question: Who is Medoro?
questions.notes: Ch. 16: Medoro is the Poodle of the Fairy with Azure Hair, sent with the coach to fetch Pinocchio hanging from the giant oak.

questions.question: How many gold pieces does Fire Eater give Pinocchio and for whom are they meant?
questions.notes: Ch. 11-12: Fire Eater gives Pinocchio five gold pieces for his father Geppetto, who is poor.

questions.question: Who hangs Pinocchio from the giant oak and who has him rescued?
questions.notes: Ch. 15-16: the Assassins (the Fox and the Cat) hang him; the Fairy with Azure Hair has him taken down.

questions.question: Which friend convinces Pinocchio to go to the Land of Toys, and what do they both turn into?
questions.notes: Ch. 30-32: Lamp-Wick convinces Pinocchio to go to the Land of Toys; after five months both grow donkey ears and turn into donkeys.

questions.question: Who buys Pinocchio the donkey after the Land of Toys, and for what purpose is he bought again later?
questions.notes: Ch. 33: the owner of a circus buys him to teach him tricks; lamed, he is sold to a man who wants his skin for a drumhead.

questions.question: Who is about to fry Pinocchio in a pan and how is he described?
questions.notes: Ch. 28: the Green Fisherman (green skin, green eyes, green beard).

questions.question: Who helps Pinocchio and Geppetto reach the shore after escaping from the Shark?
questions.notes: Ch. 35-36: the Tunny, who escaped from the Shark with them, carries Geppetto and Pinocchio on his back to the shore.

questions.question: For whom does Pinocchio work drawing water at the end of the book, and to get what?
questions.notes: Ch. 36: Pinocchio draws water from the well for Farmer John, in exchange for a glass of milk for his sick father Geppetto. (In the Italian original he turns a water wheel for Giangio.)

questions.question: With what object does Pinocchio kill the Talking Cricket?
How does the story of Pinocchio end? What does he turn into at the end?
questions.notes: Ch. 36: he becomes a real boy.

questions.question: Where does Pinocchio find his father Geppetto after searching for him for a long time?
questions.notes: Ch. 35: inside the body of the Terrible Shark.

questions.question: Summarize Pinocchio's main mistakes: why does he fall into the traps of bad friends and bad company?
questions.notes: Global question, approximate keyword grading: references to Lamp-Wick or the Fox and the Cat and to refusing school/work.
